record.final_answer:
Research shelf has one relevant fact — docs.saltmarsh.example/limits, read 2026-08-21:

- Hosted runners: a single job is cancelled after 6 hours.
- A whole pipeline run: 72 hours.
- Jobs queued more than 24 hours are dropped.
- Self-hosted runners: no job time limit.

So a 7-hour job on hosted runners gets killed around the 6-hour mark, regardless of it being nightly. Two ways it fits: split it across multiple jobs/stages with the work chained (each under 6h), or run it on a self-hosted runner. If it has to stay one job on hosted infrastructure, the limit stands.

One caveat: that page was read two months ago; worth a quick re-check before you build around it.
